question: Should `sessions.list` intentionally cap every successful request above 1000 and require existing clients to follow pagination, or must current unbounded successful requests remain available?
rationale: The patch changes externally observable gateway behavior for schema-valid requests, and the repository evidence supplied here does not show maintainer approval of the new ceiling or an established upgrade contract.

options.title: Adopt the 1000-row contract
options.body: Approve the bounded response model, document the effective-limit and pagination behavior, and retain regression coverage for callers requesting values above the cap.

options.title: Preserve unbounded requests
options.body: Keep the existing successful-result behavior and pursue a resource-control design that does not truncate already-valid direct-RPC callers.

recommendation.title: Adopt the 1000-row contract
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded response model, document the effective-limit and pagination behavior, and retain regression coverage for callers requesting values above the cap.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent gateway-bound change is the closest documented precedent in the supplied history, though ownership of this endpoint itself remains unproven.
